fixes.penalty: Late-filed returns with a balance due: a penalty of 5% per month of the balance due. Failure to pay: 1% per month, up to 25%, of the tax due, in addition to interest. Interest on late or underpaid tax: 1/2% per month from the payment due date. Separate penalties apply for negligence, fraud and substantial understatement.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Late-filed returns with a balance due are subject to a penalty of 5% per month of the balance due. ... The law provides a penalty of 1% per month (not to exceed 25%) of the net tax liabilities for failure to pay
fixes.note: Figures are from the 2025 resident instructions (revised 03/26/26).

fixes.penalty: Delinquent filing penalty (not paid by the due date and not filed by the extended due date): 5% of the amount due for each month or part of a month unpaid, from the original due date, up to 25%. If the balance due is $540 or less, the penalty is $135 or 100% of the amount due, whichever is less. Late payment: 5% of the unpaid tax plus 0.5% for each month or part of a month unpaid, up to 40 months. Interest also applies.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: 5% of the amount due ... for each month or part of a month unpaid. The maximum penalty is 25%. Individuals only: If your tax return shows a balance due of $540 or less, the penalty is either: $135 / 100% of the amount due

fixes.penalty: Late filing (without a valid extension): 5% of the tax due for each month or part of a month the return is late, up to 25%; if more than 60 days late, the minimum penalty is the lesser of $100 or the total amount due. Late payment: 0.5% of the unpaid amount per month or part of a month, up to 25%, plus interest compounded daily.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: 5% of the tax due for each month (or part of a month) the return is late, up to a maximum of 25% ... If your return is more than 60 days late, your minimum penalty is the lesser of $100 or the total amount due

fixes.penalty: Late-filing (or non-filing): the lesser of $250 or 2% of the tax required to be shown (reduced by timely payments and credits); if still not filed within 30 days of a notice of non-filing, an additional penalty of the greater of $250 or 2% of the tax shown due, up to $5,000, even when no tax is due. Late payment: 2% if 1-30 days late, 10% if 31 or more days late (higher rates after an audit begins). Interest accrues daily at the federal underpayment rate.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: The first tier rate is the lesser of $250 or two percent (2%) of the tax required to be shown on the return ... If the payment is 1 – 30 days late, the late-payment penalty rate is two percent (2%). If the payment is 31+ days late, the late-payment penalty rate is ten percent (10%).
fixes.note: Publication 103 (September 2025) sets out the uniform penalties for taxes the Department administers; income tax due must be paid by the original due date even when the filing date is extended.

fixes.penalty: Late filing (after the original or extended due date): 5% per month or part of a month, up to 25%, of the outstanding tax; a $100 penalty for each month the return is late may also be charged. Late payment: 5% of the outstanding balance. Interest: 3% above the prime rate for each month or part of a month unpaid.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: When you file a return after the original or extended due date, we will assess a penalty of 5% per month (or part of a month) up to a maximum of 25% on the outstanding tax balance. You may also be charged a $100 penalty for each month the return is late.

fixes.penalty: Filed and paid on Form IT-201, so the personal income tax penalties apply to the return: late filing 5% of the tax due per month up to 25% (minimum the lesser of $100 or the amount due if more than 60 days late); late payment 0.5% per month up to 25%; plus interest.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: 5% of the tax due for each month (or part of a month) the return is late, up to a maximum of 25% ... 0.5% of the unpaid amount for each month (or part of a month) it is not paid, up to a maximum of 25%
fixes.note: The penalty page is the State's personal income tax page; it does not mention New York City tax by name. The City tax is reported on the same IT-201 and its penalty and interest go on the same line.

fixes.confirmEvidence: To find out how much you owe, how to pay, when your return is due, the status of your refund, and how to get tax relief: Find your state's tax agency web page
fixes.note: USA.gov confirms the due date is set by, and published by, each state's tax agency. Of the state resident instructions read in this session, California, New York, Illinois and New Jersey use April 15 and Delaware uses April 30, which agrees with our wording.
fixes.notFound: The penalty is set by each state and differs from state to state; no federal or multi-state official page states one rule. The IRS State government websites page and USA.gov State and local taxes page only point to each state tax agency. For examples read in this session, see the state entries (e.g. California 5% per month up to 25%, New York 5% per month up to 25%, New Jersey 5% per month up to 25% plus $100 per month, Illinois lesser of $250 or 2%, Delaware 5% per month).

fixes.confirmEvidence: To find out how much you owe, how to pay, when your return is due ... Find your state's tax agency web page
fixes.note: USA.gov supports 'set by the state'; the claim that the nonresident return is usually due on the same date as the resident return was not checked on any state page in this session, so it stays unconfirmed.

fixes.penalty: Late-filed returns: a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. Failure to pay tax shown on a timely filed return: an additional 1% per month, up to 25%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Corporate income tax returns filed late are subject to a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. ... an additional penalty of 1% per month (not to exceed 25%) is imposed for failure to pay

fixes.penalty: Late returns: a penalty of 5% per month, up to 50% of the tax due, plus interest of 1/2% per month from the original due date until paid. Failure to pay tax shown on a timely filed return: an additional 1% per month, up to 25%. Late or short estimated payments for nonresident shareholders: 1.5% per month.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Returns filed late are subject to a penalty of 5% per month, up to a maximum of 50% of the tax liability due, plus interest of 1/2% per month from the original due date until paid.
fixes.dueText: On or before the 15th day of the 3rd month after the close of the taxable year (March 15 for a calendar year). A federal automatic six-month extension extends the Delaware filing date by six months; it does not extend payment.
fixes.confirmEvidence: File Delaware Form SCT-RTN on or before the fifteenth day of the third month following the close of the taxable year.
fixes.note: Applies to every corporation that is an S corporation for federal purposes (2025 instructions, revised 11/03/25).

fixes.penalty: Late returns: a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. Failure to pay tax shown on a timely filed return: an additional 1% per month, up to 25%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Gross receipts tax returns filed late are subject to a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. In addition ... 1% per month (not to exceed 25%)

fixes.penalty: Late returns: a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. Failure to pay tax shown on a timely filed return: an additional 1% per month, up to 25%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Gross receipts tax returns filed late are subject to a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. In addition ... 1% per month (not to exceed 25%)

fixes.penalty: No penalty for registering late is stated. Once registered, withholding returns filed late carry a penalty of 5% per month plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date, and failure to pay tax shown on a timely return an additional 1% per month, up to 25%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Withholding tax returns filed late are subject to a penalty of 5% per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month from the original due date until paid. ... 1% per month (not to exceed 25%)
fixes.note: The penalty quoted is for the withholding returns, not for the registration itself; the unemployment account (Department of Labor) was not researched.

fixes.penalty: Return not filed on time: the Department may impose a $10 penalty if the return is filed within 30 days of its delinquency notice, or $25 if not filed within 30 days of that notice (it then makes the return itself from the best information available). Underpaid tax carries interest at the average prime rate plus 4% a year (adjusted each January 1, never more than 18%). Deficiency due to negligence: 10% penalty; due to fraud: 25%. The licence can be revoked or suspended.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: The department may impose a penalty of ten dollars ($10.00) upon any vendor who fails to file his return in a timely manner ... The department may impose a penalty of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) upon any vendor who fails to file his return within thirty (30) days of receiving notice
fixes.note: Wyoming Statutes 39-15-108(b) and (c), read in the Legislature's compiled Title 39.

fixes.penalty: Return not filed on time: the Department may impose a $10 penalty if the return is filed within 30 days of its delinquency notice, or $25 if not filed within 30 days of that notice (it then makes the return itself from the best information available). Underpaid tax carries interest at the average prime rate plus 4% a year (adjusted each January 1, never more than 18%). Deficiency due to negligence: 10% penalty; due to fraud: 25%. The licence can be revoked or suspended.

The department may impose a penalty of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) upon any vendor who fails to file his return within thirty (30) days of receiving notice
fixes.note: Wyoming Statutes 39-15-108(b) and (c), read in the Legislature's compiled Title 39.

Underpaid tax carries interest at the average prime rate plus 4% a year (adjusted each January 1, never more than 18%). Deficiency due to negligence: 10% penalty; due to fraud: 25%. fixes.penalty: Unemployment insurance: contributions not paid when due bear interest of 2% per month or part of a month; an employer that has not paid everything or filed every quarterly report by September 30 is assigned a delinquent rate with a 2% increase in its base rate for the next year. Workers' compensation: a payroll report not submitted within 30 days of its due date costs 00 per delinquent report; an employer that does not apply for coverage is liable for all awards to an injured employee.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Contributions not paid on the date due shall bear interest of two percent (2%) per month ... An employer failing to submit a report required by this section within thirty (30) days of the date due shall ... be assessed a penalty of one hundred dollars (00.00) for each delinquent report.
fixes.note: No penalty specifically for registering late was found; the figures are for the reports and payments that follow (W.S. 27-3-503(b), 27-3-510(a), 27-14-202(j), 27-14-203(a)).

fixes.penalty: Delinquent filing penalty (not paid by the due date and not filed by the extended due date): 5% of the amount due for each month or part of a month unpaid, from the original due date, up to 25%. Late payment: 5% of the unpaid tax plus 0.5% for each month or part of a month unpaid, up to 40 months. Interest also applies.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Delinquent filing penalty: Individuals and businesses ... 5% of the amount due ... for each month or part of a month unpaid. The maximum penalty is 25%.

fixes.penalty: Late return: $18 for each shareholder per month, up to 12 months. Tax not paid on time: the delinquent filing penalty of 5% per month up to 25% (when also not filed by the extended due date) and the late payment penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax plus 0.5% per month, up to 40 months. Interest also applies.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: S Corporation penalty On or after January 1, 2011: $18 for each shareholder, per month (up to 12 months). RTC 19172 and RTC 19172.5

fixes.penalty: Late payment: 5% of the unpaid amount plus 0.5% for each month or part of a month unpaid, up to 40 months; for an LLC this is computed on the underpaid annual tax, LLC fee and nonconsenting nonresident tax. Interest also applies.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: 5% of the unpaid tax (underpayment), and 0.5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of the month it's unpaid not to exceed 40 months (monthly). For LLCs, the penalty is computed on the underpayment of annual tax, LLC fee

fixes.penalty: Estimated fee not paid by the 15th day of the 6th month (at least the lesser of the current year's fee or 100% of the prior year's fee): 10% of the underpaid fee. A fee still unpaid at the return due date also carries the late payment penalty (5% plus 0.5% per month, up to 40 months) and interest.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Penalty for Underpayment of Estimated LLC Fee ... Penalty 10% of the underpaid fee. RTC 17942

fixes.penalty: Late return (LLC treated as a partnership): $18 for each member per month, up to 12 months. Unpaid tax or fee: the late payment penalty of 5% plus 0.5% per month, up to 40 months, and interest.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Return late filing penalty: S corporations, partnerships, or LLCs treated as partnerships ... On or after January 1, 2011: $18 for each partner/member, per month (up to 12 months).

fixes.penalty: Delinquent filing penalty (amount due not paid by the due date and return not filed by the extended due date): 5% of the amount due per month or part of a month, up to 25%. Late payment of the $800 annual tax or the LLC fee: 5% of the unpaid amount plus 0.5% per month, up to 40 months. Interest also applies.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Delinquent filing penalty: Individuals and businesses ... 5% of the amount due ... The maximum penalty is 25%. ... For LLCs, the penalty is computed on the underpayment of annual tax, LLC fee
fixes.dueText: Single-member LLC owned by an individual or a non-pass-through entity: the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year (extended: 15th day of the 10th month). Owned by an S corporation, or by a partnership or an entity treated as a partnership: the 15th day of the 3rd month after the close of the tax year.
fixes.confirmEvidence: Single member LLC (owned by an individual or a non-pass through entity) Return due date 15th day of the 4th month after the close of your tax year.
fixes.note: The due rule given is for an SMLLC owned by an individual (the case the rule applies to: kind llc or sole_prop). An SMLLC owned by an S corporation or a partnership is due the 15th day of the 3rd month (extended: 9th month if owned by an S corporation, 10th month if owned by a partnership).

fixes.penalty: Late return: $18 for each partner per month, up to 12 months. Unpaid tax (limited partnerships and LLPs, $800 annual tax): late payment penalty of 5% plus 0.5% per month, up to 40 months, and interest.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Partnership penalty ... On or after January 1, 2011: $18 for each partner/member, per month (up to 12 months).

fixes.penalty: 10% penalty for a return not filed by its due date and 10% for a late payment; when both are late the penalty does not exceed 10% of the tax due for the period. Interest is charged for each month or fraction of a month the payment is late.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: A 10 percent penalty if you do not file your tax return by its due date. A 10 percent penalty if your tax payment is late. If you file a late return and make a late tax payment, your penalty will not exceed 10 percent of the amount of tax due

fixes.penalty: 10% penalty for a return not filed by its due date and 10% for a late payment; when both are late the penalty does not exceed 10% of the tax due for the period. Interest is charged for each month or fraction of a month the payment is late.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: A 10 percent penalty if you do not file your tax return by its due date. A 10 percent penalty if your tax payment is late. If you file a late return and make a late tax payment, your penalty will not exceed 10 percent of the amount of tax due

fixes.penalty: 10% penalty for a return not filed by its due date and 10% for a late payment; when both are late the penalty does not exceed 10% of the tax due for the period. Interest is charged for each month or fraction of a month the payment is late.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: A 10 percent penalty if you do not file your tax return by its due date. A 10 percent penalty if your tax payment is late. If you file a late return and make a late tax payment, your penalty will not exceed 10 percent of the amount of tax due

fixes.penalty: Failure to register as an employer through intentional disregard or intent to evade: $100 per unreported employee, applied in the assessed quarter with the most unreported employees. Late contributions: 15% of the late contributions; reports filed more than 60 days late: a further 15% of the late contributions and withholding.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Failure to register as an employer when the failure is due to intentional disregard or intent to evade. ... $100 per unreported employee – applied in the assessed quarter with the highest number of unreported employees.
fixes.note: From the EDD penalty reference chart, DE 231EP Rev. 3 (1-26).

fixes.penalty: Not filed when due (or invalid extension): 5% of the tax per month, up to 25%; if not filed within 60 days of the due date, at least the smaller of $100 or 100% of the tax required to be shown. Tax not paid when due: 0.5% per month, up to 25%. Interest runs from the original due date.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: If you do not file a return when due, or if the request for extension is invalid, add to the tax 5% per month up to 25% [§ 1085(a)(1)(A)]. ... add to the tax ½% per month up to a total of 25% [§ 1085(a)(2)].

fixes.penalty: Not filed when due (or invalid extension): 5% of the tax per month, up to 25%; if not filed within 60 days, at least the smaller of $100 or 100% of the tax required to be shown. Tax not paid: 0.5% per month, up to 25%. Interest from the original due date. Failure to pay estimated tax on behalf of a shareholder: $50 per shareholder for each failure.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: If you do not file a return when due or if the request for extension is invalid, add to the tax 5% per month, up to a total of 25%. See § 1085(a)(1)(A).

fixes.penalty: Late return (including extensions), or a return missing required information: $50 for each month or part of a month, up to five months, multiplied by the number of partners during the year who are individuals, estates or trusts subject to New York personal income tax.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: The penalty for each month or fraction of a month (for a maximum of five months) that the failure continues is $50 multiplied by the total number of persons who were partners in the partnership
fixes.note: The 2025 IT-204-LL instructions state that calendar-year 2025 partnership returns are due March 16, 2026 (March 15 fell on a Sunday).

fixes.penalty: The instructions say only that failing to file on time or to pay the full fee by the due date may bring penalties and interest; no amount is stated. There is no extension.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: There is no extension of time to file Form IT-204-LL or pay the annual fee. If you fail to timely file Form IT-204-LL, or fail to pay the full amount of the filing fee by the due date, you may be subject to penalties and interest.
fixes.note: No figure for this penalty was found on an official page; only the stated consequence.

fixes.penalty: Return with no tax due filed late or not at all: $50. Return up to 60 days late: 10% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% per additional month, up to 30%, minimum $50. Not filed or more than 60 days late: the greater of that amount, the lesser of $100 or 100% of the tax due, or $50. Filed on time but not paid: 10% for the first month plus 1% per month, up to 30%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: file a return late by 60 days or less. (Tax Law, sec. 1145(a)(1)(i)) 10% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% for each additional month or part of a month not to exceed 30% of the tax due. However, this penalty cannot be less than $50.
fixes.note: Tax Bulletin ST-805, issued March 26, 2010.

fixes.penalty: Return with no tax due filed late or not at all: $50. Return up to 60 days late: 10% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% per additional month, up to 30%, minimum $50. Not filed or more than 60 days late: the greater of that amount, the lesser of $100 or 100% of the tax due, or $50. Filed on time but not paid: 10% for the first month plus 1% per month, up to 30%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: file a return late by 60 days or less. (Tax Law, sec. 1145(a)(1)(i)) 10% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% for each additional month or part of a month not to exceed 30% of the tax due. However, this penalty cannot be less than $50.
fixes.note: Tax Bulletin ST-805, issued March 26, 2010.

fixes.penalty: Return with no tax due filed late or not at all: $50. Return up to 60 days late: 10% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% per additional month, up to 30%, minimum $50. Not filed or more than 60 days late: the greater of that amount, the lesser of $100 or 100% of the tax due, or $50. Filed on time but not paid: 10% for the first month plus 1% per month, up to 30%.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: file a return late by 60 days or less. (Tax Law, sec. 1145(a)(1)(i)) 10% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% for each additional month or part of a month not to exceed 30% of the tax due. However, this penalty cannot be less than $50.
fixes.note: Tax Bulletin ST-805, issued March 26, 2010.

fixes.penalty: No penalty for registering late is stated. Once liable: unpaid unemployment insurance contributions carry interest at 12% a year from the due date; a quarterly Form NYS-45 not filed by its due date carries a penalty of the greater of $1,000 or $50 times the number of employees on the last return, up to $10,000 a quarter (abated if filed within 30 days of the certified-mail notice).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: For failure to file a required form ... by the prescribed due date, the penalty imposed is equal to the greater of $1,000 or $50 multiplied by the number of employees shown on the last form filed by the employer. The maximum penalty ... is $10,000 for any one calendar quarter
fixes.note: The figures are for the quarterly returns and contributions that follow registration, not for the registration itself.

fixes.penalty: $50 for each report filed after the due date. Tax paid 1-30 days late: 5% penalty; more than 30 days late: 10% penalty. Interest on past-due tax begins 61 days after the due date.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: A $50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date. If tax is paid 1-30 days after the due date, a 5 percent penalty is assessed. If tax is paid over 30 days after the due date, a 10 percent penalty is assessed.

fixes.penalty: $50 for each report filed after the due date. Tax paid 1-30 days late: 5% penalty; more than 30 days late: 10% penalty. Interest on past-due tax begins 61 days after the due date.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: A $50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date. If tax is paid 1-30 days after the due date, a 5 percent penalty is assessed. If tax is paid over 30 days after the due date, a 10 percent penalty is assessed.

fixes.penalty: $50 for each report filed after the due date. Tax paid 1-30 days late: 5% penalty; more than 30 days late: 10% penalty. Interest on past-due tax begins 61 days after the due date.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: A $50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date. If tax is paid 1-30 days after the due date, a 5 percent penalty is assessed. If tax is paid over 30 days after the due date, a 10 percent penalty is assessed.

fixes.penalty: No penalty for registering late is stated. Late wage reports: $15 if filed within 15 days of the due date; $30 plus 0.05% of unreported wages if filed later in the first month; amounts rising for each further month up to the third month ($30 plus 0.1%, then $30 plus 0.2%, added on). Late contributions: interest of 1.5% per month, up to 37.5% of the contribution. Other violations (records, false reports, rules): $30.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: $15, if the completed report is filed not later than the 15th day after the report's due date; $30 plus one-twentieth of one percent of wages that the employer failed to report, if ... filed after the 15th day ... but during the first month
fixes.dueText: Within 10 days of becoming liable under the Texas Unemployment Compensation Act.
fixes.confirmEvidence: Texas Unemployment Compensation Act requires employers to register with the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) within 10 days of becoming liable.
fixes.note: The old sourceUrl (programs/unemployment-tax/register-new-account) now returns Page Not Found; the registration page is https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax. Liability is not simply paying the first employee; the due rule 'When you start paying employees' is close but the official wording is 'within 10 days of becoming liable'. The penalty figures are from the Act as published by TWC (Sec. 213.021 and 213.022).

fixes.penalty: Late return: 10% of any unpaid tax for each month or part of a month late, up to 50% of the unpaid tax. If no tax is due: $50 per month or part of a month, up to $300. A floating rate of interest applies to late payments; underpaid estimated tax carries a 12% per year penalty.

fixes.penalty: Late report: $25 for each 30 days or part of 30 days the report is late. A floating rate of interest applies to late payments. An erroneous or incomplete report: $50 or 10% of tax due, whichever is greater, up to $300 per report. Not filing electronically when required: $25 per report plus $1 per employee, up to $300; not paying electronically: $25 per remittance.

fixes.penalty: Late payment: a penalty on a graduated scale of 2% (up to 10 days late), 4% (11-15 days), 6% (16-20 days), 8% (21-30 days) and 10% (more than 30 days) of the tax due, plus interest of 0.75% per month or part of a month. If the Department has to make a determination because no return was filed: a 10% penalty.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: If the payment is not more than 10 days late, 2 percent of the amount of the tax or fee due. ... If the payment is more than 30 days late, 10 percent of the amount of the tax or fee due.

The Commerce Tax FAQ adds that if the tax is paid within an approved extension no penalty is imposed, but interest of 0.75% per month accrues.

fixes.penalty: No penalty for applying late is stated. After registering, the quarterly Workers' Compensation and Unemployment Insurance reports are required every quarter, even with no employees or hours, and failing to submit them results in penalties and interest (no amount stated on this page).

fixes.penalty: Late-filing (or non-filing): the lesser of $250 or 2% of the tax required to be shown (reduced by timely payments and credits); if still not filed within 30 days of a notice of non-filing, an additional penalty of the greater of $250 or 2% of the tax shown due, up to $5,000, even when no tax is due. Late payment: 2% if 1-30 days late, 10% if 31 or more days late (higher rates after an audit begins). Interest accrues daily at the federal underpayment rate.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: The first tier rate is the lesser of $250 or two percent (2%) of the tax required to be shown on the return ... If the payment is 1 – 30 days late, the late-payment penalty rate is two percent (2%). If the payment is 31+ days late, the late-payment penalty rate is ten percent (10%).
fixes.note: Publication 103 (September 2025) sets out the uniform penalties for taxes the Department administers; income tax due must be paid by the original due date even when the filing date is extended.

fixes.penalty: Late filing: 5% per month or part of a month on the underpayment, up to 25%; if no return is filed within 30 days of the first delinquency notice, 5% per month of the total tax liability, up to 25%. A penalty of $100 for each month the return is late may also be imposed. Late payment: 5% of the balance of tax paid after the due date. Interest: 3% above the average predominant prime rate for each month or part of a month unpaid, compounded annually.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Late Filing Penalty. 5% per month or part of a month on the amount of underpayment not to exceed 25% of that underpayment ... Also, a penalty of $100 for each month the return is delinquent may be imposed.

fixes.dueText: Form CBT-100S: the 15th day of the month following the month the federal corporate income tax return is originally due. For a December 31 year end that is April 15 (for example, 2025 year end: April 15, 2026); if the date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the next business day.
fixes.confirmEvidence: New Jersey Corporation Business Tax returns and payments, except estimated payments, are due the 15th day of the month following the month the federal corporate income tax return is originally due. ... Dec. 31, 2025 ... Apr 15, 2026
fixes.note: The 2025 CBT-100S schedule maps every year end to the 15th day of the 4th month after it (July 31 to Nov. 15, Dec. 31 to Apr. 15, June 30 to Oct. 15).
